title: Why Bonds Respond To The Fed, Not To Inflation
gist: Gavekal argues US bond prices are now driven almost exclusively by Fed rate expectations rather than inflation data. The 10-year yield peaked at 5.31% on October 6 and fell to 5.09% on less-hawkish-than-expected Fed comments, even as shockingly bad CPI and PPI data hit.

themes.theme: Tactical reprieve in the worst bond bear market since the 1970s

insights.claim: Gavekal argued in early October 2026 that the worst bond bear market since the 1970s was due for at least a tactical reprieve because investors were overestimating how many Fed rate hikes would come in the following year.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: If the market overprices Fed hikes, duration offers tactical upside as hike expectations get repriced lower.
insights.quote: the worst bear market for bonds since the 1970s was due for at least a tactical reprieve because investors were overestimating the number of Federal Reserve rate hikes

themes.theme: Fed expectations dominate inflation as the bond driver

insights.claim: Gavekal holds that US bond prices are currently driven almost exclusively by expectations about Federal Reserve policy, not by inflation data.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Bond investors should trade Fed communication and the expected hike path rather than inflation prints.
insights.quote: bond prices these days are driven almost exclusively by Fed expectations

insights.claim: The decline in US 10-year yields in October 2026 was caused by a series of Fed comments that were less hawkish than markets expected.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Fed speaker tone is the key catalyst to watch for the next leg in yields.

insights.claim: US bonds rallied over the two weeks to October 20, 2026 even though inflation clearly worsened, with shockingly bad US CPI and PPI data released on Wednesday, October 14.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Bonds rising through bad inflation prints shows inflation surprises alone may not push yields higher while the Fed sounds dovish.
